goal: Migrate all five Organization endpoints to a pure functional domain and Effect application layer with managed PostgreSQL and Redis resources, tenant-aware authorization, typed failures, and reusable full-stack tests.

tasks.name: Add dependencies and validated runtime configuration
inputs: Dependency and configuration requirements from design.md
Current API package scripts and Node 24/pnpm 11 toolchain
tasks.description: Add Effect 4 beta using the beta distribution tag, the Fastify 5-compatible rate-limit plugin, and ioredis. Rename the existing configuration modules to the required PascalCase basenames, extend Config with required REDIS_URL and positive-integer Organization rate-limit settings defaulting to 1000 requests and 60000 milliseconds, and update imports. Add the test Redis URL without changing production secret handling.

tests: rejects a missing Redis URL
rejects non-positive and non-integer rate-limit values
uses the documented quota and window defaults
accepts explicit valid overrides
acceptance: effect@beta, @fastify/rate-limit@^11.2.0, and ioredis@^6.0.0 resolve under Node 24, with the lockfile pinning the selected Effect beta
Config exposes validated Redis and Organization rate-limit settings
Existing package scripts remain authoritative

tasks.name: Implement the pure Organization domain
inputs: Organization vocabulary and invariants from CONTEXT.md
Functional-core and access requirements from design.md
tasks.description: Define a branded canonical Organization ID with non-throwing parsing, an immutable Organization entity using UTC Luxon DateTime values, create and update inputs with explicit preserve/replace description intent, and exhaustive platform/current access decisions. Reject an explicitly present undefined description through a non-throwing constructor. Keep all domain modules free of Effect, Fastify, TypeBox, Drizzle, PostgreSQL, configuration, and environment imports. Keep domain tests table-driven and limited to Exchequer behavior: complete access decisions, parsing, update intent, immutability, and actual UTC normalization without retesting Luxon.

tests: accepts canonical org TypeIDs
rejects malformed and wrong-prefix IDs without throwing
permits platform access to any target
permits current access only to the actor Organization
preserves an omitted description and replaces a supplied description
rejects an explicitly present undefined description without throwing
keeps Organization timestamps immutable under Luxon transformations
acceptance: Organization IDs are branded and can only be constructed through validated constructors or the injected generator
The Organization value and its UTC Luxon timestamps are immutable
Absent descriptions are represented as undefined
Domain dependency boundaries are pure

tasks.name: Define Effect capabilities and Organization use cases
inputs: Organization domain types from T2
Repository operations, access matrix, and error model from design.md
tasks.description: Add constructor-injected OrganizationRepo, OrganizationIdGenerator, and OrganizationService classes whose methods return Effects, with separate Effect 4 Context.Service tags and small Layers for runtime wiring. Represent repository absence with Effect Option rather than null or transport errors. Implement list, get, create, update, and delete Effects with explicit actor ID and access mode, target checks before repository calls, SQL list-scope intent, deterministic ID injection, and operation-specific application and infrastructure failure unions. OrganizationHasDependents applies only to delete; OrganizationNotFound applies only to get, update, and delete. Supply typed vi.mocked port implementations through Layer.succeed in service tests. Test only orchestration, arguments, non-invocation, absence conversion, generated IDs, and operation-specific error eligibility; do not cross every infrastructure error with every operation.

tests: covers all five use cases with vi.mocked port implementations supplied through test Layers
passes all-scope or actor-scope intent to list
gives platform access precedence when both modes are present
denies current-target mismatches before repository invocation
maps permitted get, update, and delete absence to OrganizationNotFound
propagates applicable infrastructure failures and delete-dependent failures through precise Effect error channels
allows create only for platform access and uses the injected ID generator
acceptance: Every use case accepts the actor Organization ID explicitly
Service and repository capability methods return operation-specific typed Effects
Application modules do not run Effects or import HTTP and SQL adapters
No automatic generated-ID retry is introduced

tasks.name: Introduce PostgreSQL capability and ownership Layers
inputs: Current Drizzle schema and DrizzleDB type
Resource ownership rules from design.md
tasks.description: Define the Drizzle database capability. Provide a scoped production Layer that owns one PostgreSQL pool and a test Layer that wraps an externally supplied database without owning it. Keep shutdown bounded and infallible: force-release checked-out clients after the graceful deadline, log cleanup failures, and always detach pool listeners. Keep the existing schema authoritative and add no migration.

tests: production Layer finalization closes its pool exactly once
rejected or timed-out pool shutdown forces checked-out clients closed and completes
test Layer finalization does not close an injected database or pool
acceptance: Database access is available through an Effect 4 Context.Service
Production and test ownership are explicit
No schema or migration files change

tasks.name: Implement the live Organization PostgreSQL adapter
inputs: OrganizationsTable and Drizzle database capability
OrganizationRepo contract and typed error vocabulary
tasks.description: Implement the repository Layer with Organization-ID ordering, optional actor filtering, limit and offset, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE RETURNING, database-owned timestamps decoded to immutable UTC Luxon DateTime values, conditional description assignment from explicit preserve/replace intent, and safe row decoding. Translate connectivity failures to retryable repository unavailability, invalid rows to persistence decoding failures, unexpected SQL failures to sanitized persistence errors, and delete error 23503 to OrganizationHasDependents. Do not synthesize name conflicts. Isolate database fixtures, reserve direct adapter tests for SQL and decoding contracts, and test rare failures deterministically without terminating PostgreSQL backends or deliberately aborting transactions.

tests: orders lists by Organization ID and applies limit and offset
filters current-Organization lists in PostgreSQL
creates rows with database timestamps and decodes RETURNING values
preserves or replaces descriptions according to update input
returns explicit absence for missing get, update, and delete
maps a real dependent Ledger delete to OrganizationHasDependents
allows duplicate Organization names
maps invalid persisted rows and rejected database operations into typed failures
acceptance: Drizzle and SQL values do not escape the adapter
All rejected promises are captured in the Effect error channel
Delete uses the database foreign-key constraint as the source of truth

tasks.name: Add Redis and ID-generator live Layers
inputs: Redis failure policy from design.md
OrganizationIdGenerator capability from T3
tasks.description: Add the canonical TypeID generator Layer and a scoped ioredis capability configured from REDIS_URL with bounded connection and command retries and no indefinitely queued requests. Make the Redis finalizer attempt graceful shutdown and always disconnect without hanging. Provide non-owning test Layers for injected clients.

tests: generated IDs satisfy the domain smart constructor
Redis acquisition does not require Redis readiness for unrelated routes
owned Redis finalization is bounded and runs once
injected test clients are not closed by non-owning Layers
acceptance: The runtime can expose one Redis client per server
Redis command failures are observable by the HTTP rate limiter
No unbounded shutdown or request retry behavior remains

tasks.name: Compose one managed runtime and bridge legacy repositories
inputs: Live and test Layers from T3 through T6
Existing Fastify plugin registration and shutdown behavior
tasks.description: Expose the Organization public contract and composed Layer through organizations/index.ts, then compose configuration, PostgreSQL, Redis, and that Layer into one ManagedRuntime per buildServer call. Rename the shared server and application entry-point modules to PascalCase, update imports and package entry commands, and permit buildServer to accept a complete runtime Layer for tests while always creating and disposing the runtime itself through one shared disposal promise. Retrieve the runtime-owned Drizzle database for legacy repositories, make RepoPlugin a purely injected-database bridge, and remove its pool creation, five-second delay, and close hook. Configure migrated-slice imports to use index.ts and explicit dependency edges.

tests: repeated requests use the same runtime and resource instances
server shutdown disposes the runtime exactly once
cross-slice deep imports into Organizations fail boundary lint
legacy repositories receive the runtime-owned Drizzle database
external test resources remain open after runtime disposal
acceptance: Exactly one ManagedRuntime is created per Fastify server
Cross-slice imports use the Organization index while concrete Live modules remain private
No runtime is constructed per request
The artificial repository shutdown delay and duplicate pool ownership are removed

tasks.name: Add Organization schemas, authorization, and Effect error handling
inputs: Current JWT role and permission model
Organization API and error contracts from design.md
tasks.description: Add Organization-specific TypeBox schemas so stricter pagination does not alter Ledger routes. Rename the shared authentication and error modules to PascalCase and update their imports. Expose each verified token's permission set while preserving the existing all-permissions behavior of hasPermissions. Derive platform/current access with platform precedence. Translate omitted or supplied description fields into explicit domain update intent and map an explicitly present undefined description to 400. Add an edge-only Effect runner and exhaustive operation-specific tagged-error mapping using the request URL and request ID; log and sanitize decoding failures, persistence failures, and defects.

tests: maps every expected tagged error to its designed status and RFC 7807 schema
returns 403 for current-target mismatch and 404 for permitted absence
uses request.url and request.id for instance and traceId
logs unexpected causes and returns a sanitized 500
derives platform access before current access when both permissions exist
preserves existing non-Organization permission semantics
acceptance: Organization pagination accepts only offset integers >= 0 and limit integers from 1 through 100
HTTP validation and authentication remain adapter concerns
Expected failures are handled exhaustively before the runtime edge

tasks.name: Add the shared Redis-backed Organization limiter
inputs: Runtime-owned Redis client
Manual limiter API and rate-limit configuration from design.md
tasks.description: Register @fastify/rate-limit with global false, skipOnError false, the runtime client, the configured quota and window, the stable environment namespace, and actor-ID key generation. Create one manual limiter shared by all Organization routes. Convert allowed results to limit, remaining, and reset headers; exceeded results to a tagged 429 with Retry-After; and store failures to a tagged 503.

tests: all authenticated Organization operations use the same actor bucket
invalid authentication never invokes the limiter
allowed responses include limit, remaining, and reset headers
exceeded responses include Retry-After and tagged 429 details
store failures become sanitized tagged 503 failures
acceptance: The Redis key is exchequer:<environment>:organizations:<actor-organization-id>
Health, documentation, Ledger, and other routes do not receive a rate-limit hook
Redis failures fail Organization routes closed

tasks.name: Replace the Organization routes
inputs: Organization service capability
Organization schemas, authorization resolver, limiter, and Effect runner
tasks.description: Register the flat Organization HTTP adapter at the existing prefix. Apply JWT authentication, rate limiting, access-mode derivation, one application use case, and response serialization in that order. Implement 201 with Location, 204 with no body, absent-description omission, and exact OpenAPI error sets. Remove Organization from the legacy service container and remove the old mocked route and service implementation.

tests: all five routes invoke the managed runtime instead of server.services
create returns 201, the created representation, and a canonical Location header
delete returns 204 with an empty body
description is omitted when absent
schemas advertise only applicable statuses and reserve 409 for delete
OpenAPI response schemas match runtime response shapes
acceptance: All existing Organization paths and JSON field names remain stable
Create requires organization:write
List and get use organization:read or my:organization:read
Update and delete use organization:write or my:organization:write

tasks.name: Establish the reusable HTTP-to-PostgreSQL harness
inputs: buildServer and live Organization Layers
JWT signer, test PostgreSQL database, and Compose-managed Valkey
tasks.description: Build a reusable harness that composes real PostgreSQL with an externally owned Redis test Layer, starts buildServer, signs actor JWTs, injects HTTP requests, creates isolated unique fixtures, and cleans them in reverse dependency order without truncation. Rename the test setup and Vitest configuration modules to PascalCase, update every configuration reference and package command, and add full-stack Organization coverage with no mocked service or repository. Use one assembled CRUD journey plus targeted public-contract cases instead of replaying the complete repository matrix.

tests: covers all five success paths, response bodies, headers, and post-delete absence
covers platform and current access plus platform precedence
verifies tenant-filtered lists and cross-tenant 403 before existence lookup
covers malformed IDs, invalid pagination and bodies, authentication, and missing rows
verifies duplicate names remain valid
verifies a real dependent Ledger delete returns 409
checks generated OpenAPI against the contracts exercised at runtime
acceptance: The harness exercises the real Fastify-to-PostgreSQL lifecycle
Services and repositories are not mocked
Fixture cleanup is isolated and never truncates shared tables
The harness is reusable by later Effect resource migrations

tasks.name: Verify distributed limiting and resource lifecycle
inputs: Compose-managed Valkey
Injectable runtime Layers and the full-stack test harness
tasks.description: Add integration tests using unique environment namespaces. Start two independent Fastify servers against the same Redis service, exhaust one actor's shared bucket across both, verify actor isolation, and exercise fail-closed behavior. Add deterministic lifecycle regressions for runtime-owned and externally injected resources without elapsed-time assertions or forced infrastructure termination.

tests: shares quota consumption across two server instances
isolates buckets for different actors
verifies allowed and exceeded headers plus Retry-After
verifies invalid JWTs do not consume a valid actor bucket
maps an injected failing store to sanitized 503
keeps health and Ledger routes available while Redis is unavailable
finalizes PostgreSQL and Redis once without the old delay
does not close injected external resources
acceptance: Distributed rate limiting behaves consistently across API instances
Organization routes fail closed when Redis fails
Server shutdown remains bounded and resource-safe

tasks.name: Remove obsolete Organization production code and run quality gates
inputs: Completed flat Organization vertical slice
Existing unrelated repository tests and legacy OrgID consumers
tasks.description: Remove the transport-coupled Organization repository and entity from production wiring and delete their obsolete tests. Replace their use in unrelated repository test setup with a fixture-only PostgreSQL helper while preserving those tests' behavior and the legacy OrgID type used by unmigrated resources. Remove stale exports and Organization fixtures no longer used by routes, then execute the complete validation sequence.

tests: runs focused Organization domain, service, adapter, HTTP, Redis, and lifecycle tests
runs the complete @exchequerio/api test suite
runs pnpm run check
runs pnpm run ci under Node 24
acceptance: No production Organization endpoint imports legacy route, service, repository, or entity modules
Unmigrated resources retain their current interfaces and behavior
No artificial Organization resource ownership or shutdown delay remains
No database migration, web, docs-site, shared-package, or CONTEXT.md change is introduced
The final diff contains only approved scope and preserves unrelated work
